en.one: Owner of the Chili's and Maggiano's restaurants. Profit tripled in three years, but the advantage is new and easily overcome. Did not pass Wall 3.
en.business: Brinker International operates and franchises Chili's Grill & Bar and Maggiano's Little Italy restaurants in the US. At 24 June 2026 it had 1,635 restaurants: 1,163 company-owned and 472 franchised. It earns its money from food and drink sales in its own restaurants: in fiscal 2026 revenue was 5.81 billion dollars and net profit 487.0 million. Franchise revenue is, in the company's own words, not material. The fiscal year ends in late June.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass Wall 3. The advantage is real but new: comparable restaurant sales at Chili's rose 25.3% in fiscal 2025 and 9.2% in fiscal 2026, and 10.1% in the latest quarter. The operating margin went from 5.2% in 2024 to 10.7% in 2026; net profit rose from 155.3 million dollars to 487.0 million. But this result is won again every year with price, menu and advertising: advertising expense rose from 130.2 million dollars to 163.6 million in two years. Nothing ties the customer in; the company itself describes the industry as "highly competitive as to price, service, restaurant location, convenience" and says casual dining has not seen significant growth in customer traffic in recent years. Sales at the same company's second brand, Maggiano's, are falling (−3.4% in the latest quarter). Return on invested capital was 8.7% in fiscal 2023 and is 25.9% today. Real return on equity was 179% and 112% in the last two fiscal years and 126% over the last 12 months, but these figures are high because they are divided by a very small equity. Equity was negative in the three years before that. This filter does not count an advantage that has to be defended anew every year as a moat.
en.mgmt: The company pays no dividend: none was declared in fiscal 2025 or 2026. Profit goes to buybacks and to the restaurants: in fiscal 2026 it bought back 2.9 million shares for 400.0 million dollars (net profit 487.0 million) and capital expenditure was 231.9 million. In August 2026 the buyback authorisation was raised to 750 million dollars. In July 2026 the 350 million dollars of 8.25% notes were redeemed early with borrowings under the credit line. The company also bought 12 Chili's restaurants from a franchisee for about 27.5 million dollars. Equity is small (399.9 million dollars) because most of the profit has gone to buybacks for years.
en.latest: 28 October 2026: In the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (ended 23 September 2026) revenue was 1,475.6 million dollars (1,349.2 million a year earlier), net profit 113.3 million (99.5 million) and earnings per share 2.64 dollars (2.17). Comparable restaurant sales at Chili's rose 10.1% and traffic 6.4%; sales at Maggiano's fell 3.4%. Profit includes a 17.6 million dollar loss on early repayment of debt. The company raised its 2027 outlook: revenue of 6.23–6.33 billion dollars and adjusted earnings per share of 13.30–13.90 dollars (previously 12.60–13.40). The year has 53 weeks; the extra week adds about 0.70 dollars to earnings per share. 125.0 million dollars of shares were bought back in the quarter.
risks: The jump in profit rests on the sales growth at Chili's over the last three years. Customers can easily move to another chain; the operating margin was 5.2% in fiscal 2024.
Equity is very small (399.9 million dollars) and was negative in the three years before. Return on equity therefore overstates the true return of the business.
The restaurant business is cyclical. Management says consumers are under pressure from inflation and gas prices; food and labour costs can also squeeze profit.
The company's 2027 earnings outlook is for a 53-week year. The contribution of the extra week (about 0.70 dollars per share) will not be there the year after.

en.one: A sports and yoga clothing brand. Narrow moat; it passed the quality walls. Profit is falling: guidance was cut twice and recent profit includes a one-off tariff refund.
en.business: lululemon designs sports and yoga clothing under its own brand and sells it in its own stores and on its own website. In fiscal 2025 (ended 1 February 2026) revenue was 11.10 billion dollars and net profit 1.58 billion dollars. Of revenue, 7.85 billion dollars (about 71%) came from the Americas and 1.75 billion dollars from China. Stores brought in 5.05 billion dollars of sales and the website 4.92 billion dollars. It had 825 stores on 2 August 2026.
en.moat_text: The moat is narrow. The advantage comes from the brand and from selling the product directly, in its own stores. It shows in the numbers: gross margin was 56.6% in fiscal 2025 and operating margin 19.9%; real return on equity has not fallen below 24.8% in five years (26.2% in the last 12 months). The moat is not counted as wide, because the advantage rests on a single brand and is weakening now. Comparable sales in the Americas fell 12% in the last quarter. Gross margin went from 59.2% in 2024 to 56.6% in 2025; the company puts this down to tariffs and more markdowns. In clothing there is no contract or switching cost that holds the customer; if fashion moves, the brand's strength moves with it.
en.mgmt: The shares are widely held. Founder Chip Wilson owns about 8.7%; he is not in management. In 2026 Wilson nominated directors; on 26 May 2026 he reached an agreement with the company and two independent directors joined the board. Chief executive Calvin McDonald left on 31 January 2026; Heidi O'Neill started on 8 September 2026. At the annual meeting of 25 June 2026, 63.2% of votes went against the pay policy. The company pays no dividend; profit goes to store investment and buybacks. It bought back 1.2 billion dollars of shares in fiscal 2025 and 695 million dollars in the first half of 2026 (at an average of 141 dollars; the price today is 106 dollars). There is no interest-bearing debt; on 2 August 2026 cash was 1.39 billion dollars and lease liabilities 2.14 billion dollars. The fiscal year ends at the end of January.
en.latest: 3 September 2026: In the second quarter of fiscal 2026 (ended 2 August) revenue fell 4% to 2.42 billion dollars. Comparable sales fell 9%; 12% in the Americas. Net profit was 329 million dollars (371 million a year earlier) and earnings per share 2.92 dollars (3.10 a year earlier). Of this, 0.86 dollars is one-off: 134.5 million dollars of refunds of cancelled tariffs and 4.1 million dollars of interest came in. Excluding the refund, earnings per share come to 2.06 dollars (our arithmetic). The company cut its full-year guidance for the second time: revenue of 10.35-10.50 billion dollars (down 5-7%) and earnings per share of 9.48-9.73 dollars (including the refund; 13.26 in 2025). Guidance for the third quarter is 0.93-0.98 dollars.
risks: Profit is falling and the calculation rests on the last 12 months: earnings per share were 12.15 dollars in the last 12 months, while the company's guidance for fiscal 2026 is 9.48-9.73 dollars. Of that, 0.86 dollars is a one-off tariff refund; excluding it the range is 8.62-8.87 dollars. Guidance was cut twice in 2026 (March: 12.10-12.30; June: 10.95-11.15). If profit falls further, the margin of safety shrinks.
The Americas: about 71% of revenue comes from here and comparable sales fell 12% in the last quarter. It is not yet clear whether the decline is temporary or lasting.
China: it was the source of growth (revenue +29% in 2025). In the last quarter revenue fell 2% in constant currency; management said the result was well below its expectations.

Tariffs and markdowns: tariffs and the end of the small-parcel exemption reduced gross profit by about 275 million dollars in 2025 (before mitigation). The removal of the exemption is in force; if markdowns rise, the margin narrows further.
Change of management: the chief executive changed in September 2026 and four new directors joined the board in 2026. Whether the new plan will work is not known.

en.one: Maker of engines and power systems for generators and industrial equipment. Passed the quality walls; did not pass Wall 3 because the moat is weak.
en.business: Power Solutions International (PSI) designs and builds emission-certified engines and power systems and sells them to equipment makers. It has three markets: power systems (generator packages for data centers and oil and gas fields), industrial (forklifts, construction equipment) and transportation. In the first nine months of 2026 net sales were 483.2 million dollars; 382.0 million came from power systems. Net sales in 2025 were 722.4 million dollars.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak; this is why the company did not pass Wall 3. There is an advantage: emission-certified engine packages that run on several fuels, and engine supply from Weichai. But the numbers do not show pricing power. Gross margin was 29.5% in 2024, fell to 25.6% in 2025 and to 21.9% in its last quarter; the company says data center products carry lower margins than oil and gas products. Sales depend on a few large buyers: four customers made 53% of 2025 sales (20%, 13%, 10% and 10% in the company's note). Real return on equity was 216.7% in 2024, 88.4% in 2025 and 30.7% in the last 12 months; these high figures come from a very small equity base: according to the source, equity was negative until 2023.
en.mgmt: Weichai America owns about 46.0% of the shares and holds a majority of the board with four seats. PSI buys engines from Weichai: inventory purchases were 31.1 million dollars in the first nine months of 2026; there is a minimum purchase commitment of 290.1 million dollars in total through 2029 with Weichai affiliate SWIEC. The collaboration agreement with Weichai expired on 20 March 2026; its renewal is under negotiation. Profit goes to paying down debt: the revolving credit balance was 95.0 million dollars at the end of 2025 and 35.0 million on 30 September 2026. The documents we read show no dividend or buyback program. On 9 January 2026 the company bought steel enclosure maker MTL for 11.1 million dollars. The former chief executive left in May 2026; the new one took office on 17 August 2026. A securities class action was filed against the company on 20 March 2026.
en.latest: 5 November 2026: in the third quarter of 2026 net sales were 202.1 million dollars (203.8 a year earlier), net income 29.9 million dollars (27.6) and EPS 1.30 dollars (1.20). Gross margin was 29.7%; about 1.9 points of it came from a 3.8 million dollar tariff refund that is not expected to recur. In the nine months net sales fell 9% to 483.2 million dollars, net income was 54.1 million dollars (97.9 a year earlier) and EPS 2.34 dollars (4.25). Last year's profit included a one-off benefit from the release of a tax valuation allowance; pre-tax income fell from 80.7 million dollars to 72.3 million. The company expects second-half sales to exceed last year's second half; it gives no profit guidance for the year.
risks: Profit is falling: EPS in the first nine months of 2026 dropped from 4.25 dollars to 2.34 dollars; oil and gas demand is soft and the company says this will continue.
Sales depend on a few customers: three customers made 47% of third-quarter sales. If one cuts its orders, profit falls at once.
Growth rests on data center demand; these products carry lower margins and the company does not predict a sales level for future periods.

en.one: A chain of natural and organic grocery stores. It passed the quality walls; with customer visits and profit guidance falling, the moat was judged weak and it failed Wall 3.
en.business: Sprouts runs grocery stores in the US focused on fresh, natural and organic food. On 27 September 2026 it had 504 stores in 25 states. In 2025 net sales were 8.8 billion dollars and net profit 524 million dollars. In the last quarter of 2025 about 26% of sales came from its own label (Sprouts Brand) and about 15.5% from online orders. The fiscal year ends in late December (28 December in 2025); fiscal 2026 has 53 weeks.
en.moat_text: The moat is weak. The advantage comes from the product range and the own label: gross margin was 38.8% in 2025, and real return on equity has been between 18.2% and 34.8% over five years, 28.7% in the last 12 months. But this advantage was tested in 2026 and did not hold. Comparable store sales have fallen for three quarters (−0.9% in the third quarter); according to TIKR the number of transactions fell 3.3%. The company cut its earnings per share guidance from 5.28-5.44 dollars at the start of the year to about 4.80 dollars and said it will cut prices in January. In the same period Costco and Walmart grew their sales. Grocery has many large competitors; Sprouts has no cost advantage and has not been able to hold its price premium. That is why the B score is 1; the company did not pass Wall 3.
en.mgmt: The shares trade on Nasdaq. The company pays no dividend; profit goes to new stores and share buybacks. In 2025 it bought back 4.0 million shares for 472 million dollars, and in the first nine months of 2026 another 299 million dollars. These purchases were made far above today's price (51 dollars): about 118 dollars a share on average in 2025. It will open 42 net new stores in 2026; capital spending is about 310 million dollars. Nothing is drawn on the 600 million dollar credit line. A management change was announced on 1 September 2026: Nick Konat becomes chief executive on 4 January 2027, and Jack Sinclair, chief executive since 2019, becomes executive chairman.
en.latest: 28 October 2026: in the third quarter (13 weeks ended 27 September) net sales were 2.30 billion dollars (+5%), comparable store sales −0.9%, net profit 113.4 million dollars (120.1 a year earlier) and earnings per share 1.21 dollars (1.22). In the nine months net profit was 406.3 million dollars (433.8) and earnings per share 4.30 dollars (4.38). The company cut its full-year guidance: on a 52-week basis, earnings per share of about 4.80 dollars (previously 5.32-5.40; 5.31 in 2025) and operating profit of about 605 million dollars (previously 675-685). For the fourth quarter it expects comparable sales to fall 2%-4% and earnings per share of 0.47-0.51 dollars (0.92 a year earlier). The share fell 23% the next day.
risks: Profit is falling: the company expects earnings per share of 0.47-0.51 dollars in the fourth quarter (0.92 a year earlier). The last 12 months' profit (5.22 dollars) overstates today's earning power; that is why the P/E looks low.
The price cuts planned for January 2027 may push gross margin (38.2% in the third quarter; 38.7% a year earlier) lower still; if customers do not return, profit falls from both sides.
Competitors such as Walmart, Costco and Kroger are far larger; while Sprouts' sales fell, Walmart and Costco grew their comparable sales.
The company is opening 42 net new stores in 2026; while sales at existing stores fall, new rent and fixed costs squeeze profit.
The chief executive changes on 4 January 2027; the new management's pricing and growth decisions are not yet tested.
